date: last-modified

This site characterizes the Cal-Adapt Analytics Engine downscaled climate data —
**WRF** (dynamical) and **LOCA2** (statistical/hybrid) — variable by variable, and
states plainly what each is good for.

It is produced by the **Data Quality & Documentation Pillar**, and its guiding
principle is:

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Document, don't fix.** This pillar characterizes the data and discloses what is
known. Where a question is open, the deliverable is a clear statement of the issue
and its likely cause — *not* its resolution.
:::

---

## Variables covered

| variable | status | headline |
|---|---|---|
| [**Wind speed**](variables/wind-speed.qmd) | complete, in review | Unbiased at well-sited stations; distribution too narrow, so **power density is under-predicted by 13–19 %** and high-wind days by a factor of four |
| [**Relative humidity**](variables/relative-humidity.qmd) | complete | **The verdict splits by product.** WRF-ERA5 is usable for fire weather; LOCA2 finds a third of the critical days and no simple correction repairs it |

Temperature, precipitation and snow are candidates for the next pass.

Alongside the variables, the [catalog audit](guidance/catalog-audit.qmd)
characterizes the archive's **metadata**: 1,961 findings across 390 datasets,
**276 of them errors**, and two codes on WRF's wind components account for 208.

---

## How to use this site

**If you want a verdict for your use case** → the
[good/bad matrix](guidance/good-bad-matrix.qmd). Good-for, use-with-caution, or
not-recommended, per variable × use case, with the evidence behind each.

**If you have a variable name in hand and want to know what it is** → the
[variable cards](guidance/variable-cards.qmd). One card per variable: definition,
source, transformations, known issues.

**If you want to know what happened to the number before it reached you** → the
[provenance flowchart](method/provenance.qmd). The plain-language path from global
model to delivered value, with the known gaps marked.

**If you want to know whether the catalog itself is sound** → the
[catalog audit](guidance/catalog-audit.qmd). Metadata quality across the whole
`cadcat` archive, checked through two independent access paths — because a
requirement can fail in the published store and pass in what users receive, or
the reverse.

**If you want the evidence** → the per-variable characterization pages linked
above, and the [references](references.qmd).

## The method in one page

Every variable is characterized the same way, so results are comparable across
variables and the work is repeatable. Full detail in
[Scope & Definitions](method/scope-and-definitions.qmd).

### Six quality dimensions

Each variable is scored on all six, against the reference that can actually
adjudicate it:

1. **Mean bias** — is the level right?
2. **Spatial pattern fidelity** — are the maxima in the right places?
3. **Response to terrain** — does the product resolve what its resolution implies?
4. **Diurnal and seasonal structure** — is the timing right?
5. **Extremes and distribution shape** — is the *shape* right, not just the mean?
6. **Inter-variable consistency** — is it coherent with the other variables an
   index needs?

### Three references, ordered by what each can settle

| tier | answers | cannot answer |
|---|---|---|
| **point observations** | Is the product right where we measured? | ocean, unobstructed high terrain |
| **independent fine-scale model** | Do independent models agree with each other? | whether either is right |
| **reanalysis** | Where and when do coarse and fine fields diverge? | which one is correct |

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Observations first, reanalysis last.** A ratio against a coarse reanalysis
measures a *distance*, not an error. Leading with it invites reading a resolution
difference as a defect — which is exactly what an earlier version of the wind
analysis did, attributing a 30 % offset to bias correction when it was resolution.
:::

### The finding that recurs

**Both variables so far pass on level and fail on shape.** Products look correct
on the mean — the number most often reported — and their distributions are too
narrow, which is what downstream users actually depend on.

That is why every characterization here includes a quantile comparison and a
threshold sweep, not just a bias.

---

## Definition of done, per variable

A variable is complete when all of the following exist and were produced through
the template: lit-review rows; a provenance flowchart; a characterization page
covering the six dimensions; matrix rows, filled and IOU-vetted; and a variable
card. Then the template is stamped onto the next variable.

*Source of record for evidence IDs (R##/Q##/DQ##) is the internal lit-review
database — see [References](references.qmd).*
